commits.message:
fix(ci): repair the cargo-deny config so the security audit actually runs

The security workflow has failed 11 out of 11 runs since it was added in #293
on 2026-07-27, on main as well as on pull requests. Every run failed while
deserializing deny.toml, before a single dependency was examined, so the repo
has had no vulnerability, license or supply-chain auditing at all — only the
appearance of it. It surfaces on dependency PRs because security.yml has a
paths filter for Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock.

deny.toml was written against an older cargo-deny schema and never validated
against the action that consumes it, and EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@v2 is
a floating tag, so the two drifted apart unnoticed:

- `[advisories]` `vulnerability`, `unsound` and `notice` were removed from the
  schema. Those advisories are now unconditional errors, acceptable only via an
  `ignore` entry — stricter than the levels they replace, not weaker.
- `[advisories] unmaintained` became a scope enum. Set to "workspace", the
  upstream default: "all" reaches transitive dependencies this project cannot
  act on.
- `[licenses]` `unlicensed` and `copyleft` were removed. The `allow` list is now
  exhaustive, so unlicensed crates and copyleft licenses are denied by omission.

With the config parsing, the check runs for the first time and reports clean
advisories, bans and sources. Two license findings, both addressed here:

- generate-lint-docs declared no license, unlike its two sibling crates. Added
  `license = "Apache-2.0"` to match them and the repository LICENSE.
- rustc_apfloat is `Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception`, reached transitively
  through the rustc/clippy internals. Allowed: the exception only removes a
  restriction, making it strictly more permissive than the plain Apache-2.0
  already allowed.

Also dropped the `ISC` allowance, which matched no dependency in the graph.

Verified locally with cargo-deny 0.20.2:
  advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok
